title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typewritten page, printed upside down relative to the scan, headed 'n° 382 — 78 —'. It is almost certainly a page of a Bourbaki draft (rédaction n° 382) on differential and analytic manifolds, section 7.1 on jets. Grothendieck used its blank verso as scrap paper. The neighbouring handwritten pages (Dieudonné modules, Lubin–Tate lifting of Barsotti–Tate groups with A-action) are on the other side or on other sheets and are unrelated in content.

The typed mathematics is the standard Ehresmann theory of jets:
- (end of 7.1.2) The principal-part map p^k_x : C^r_x(X) → P^k_x(X), from germs of C^r functions at x to their k-jets, is a K-algebra homomorphism.
- (7.1.3) For f defined near x with f(x) = y and h defined near y, j^k_x(h∘f) depends only on j^k_x(f) and j^k_y(h). This gives an associative composition of jets, i.e. the groupoid-like category of k-jets. A jet u is invertible if it has a two-sided inverse jet. For k = 0 every jet is invertible. For k ≥ 1, u is invertible iff it is the k-jet of a local diffeomorphism, and then every representative is a local isomorphism at x. Invertible k-jets of X into K^p (resp. with source x) are 'repères d'ordre k', i.e. Ehresmann's k-th order frames, forming R^k(X) (resp. R^k_x(X)). Open subsets give canonical inclusions J^k(U,V) ⊂ J^k(X,Y) and R^k(U) ⊂ R^k(X).
- (7.1.4) For k' ≤ k there are surjective truncation maps J^k → J^{k'}, R^k → R^{k'} and P^k → P^{k'}; the last is an algebra homomorphism.
- (7.1.5, begins) For f : U ⊂ K^p → K^q, j^k_x(f) is determined by x and the partial derivatives Δ_α f^i(x) for |α| ≤ k.

This is textbook material (Ehresmann 1951–53; Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques, Fascicule de résultats, section on jets).
errors: No mathematical errors. The statements implicitly assume k ≤ r for C^r morphisms, and r ≥ 1 for the local-isomorphism criterion. Calling invertible jets from X to K^p 'repères' is a coframe-type convention; Ehresmann often uses jets from K^p (source 0) to X. This is a convention, not an error.
